analysis:
The PR changes only Markdown: docs/operations/model-revisions.md, the new docs/reports/2026-10-15-bonsai9b-publication.md, and one index link in docs/reports/README.md. It touches no provider, coordinator, attestation or encryption code, no TB-002/TB-009/TB-011 boundary, and no App Attest authorization.

Security-relevant content:
- The runbook adds a registry-only path, the Register Model workflow with publish_revision_only=true (head lines 16-34, 114-119). It uses only MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY and no R2 credentials. It states that the coordinator validates the canonical manifest and file sizes, and that providers verify file hashes. That matches the existing weight-integrity model (T-012, T-027, A-004).
- The runbook separates upload credentials from registration credentials and tells operators not to reuse release-artifact credentials for the model bucket (head lines 44-48, 55-74). It also says not to put secrets in output. This is a least-privilege improvement.
- The incident report (head lines 34-36) discloses a temporary, explicitly authorized insert-only direct registry recovery. It labels direct database insertion as not recommended, and the runbook says not to include DB edits in routine workflow. It contains no secrets. It cites public run URLs and a public manifest hash.
- The report claims the one-off Bonsai upload path using release credentials is removed. The workflow or CI files are not in this diff, so that claim and the publish_revision_only implementation cannot be verified here.

No concrete regression or invalidated threat assumption is visible in the supplied files. Later passes should check any companion workflow change for these points: the publishing key is not exposed in logs; revision-only registration cannot register arbitrary manifest URLs; and the coordinator keeps the canonical-prefix and size checks the docs describe. No threat-model update is required for this documentation-only change.
